title: Social Stratification and Systemic Inequality
text:
Social stratification refers to the system by which a society ranks categories of people into a hierarchy. Unlike mere differences in wealth, true stratification involves durable systems that allocate resources—such as education, healthcare, and political power—unequally across various groups.

The concept challenges simple explanations of meritocracy, arguing instead that cumulative advantage and systemic barriers often dictate life chances regardless of individual talent or effort. These structures ensure that initial disadvantages frequently compound over time, leading to deeply entrenched class divisions.
